help.faq.0.0.a: Sakura is a PlayStation One frontend and emulator built on top of a Beetle PSX core for iPhone and iPad.
help.faq.1.0.q: Where do I put my files?
help.faq.1.0.a: Open the Files app and go to On My iPhone/iPad → Sakura. Drop BIOS files in `bios/` and games in `Games/`. You can also use the in-app Import button.
help.faq.1.1.a: CUE/BIN, CHD, PBP, M3U, ISO, and compressed formats like gzip or ZSO.
help.faq.1.2.a: You need a real PS1 BIOS (`.bin` or `.rom`). Put it in the `bios/` folder and select it in Settings → General.
help.faq.1.3.a:
BIOS file names and hashes for the same core family as Sakura are documented here: [Beetle PSX HW](https://docs.libretro.com/library/beetle_psx_hw/) and [Mednafen PSX firmware](https://mednafen.github.io/documentation/psx.html).

To rip CDs you own to cue/bin on Windows, try Media Preservation Frontend: [MPF releases](https://github.com/SabreTools/MPF/releases). Choose the Sony PlayStation profile.

Verification catalogs: [redump.org](https://redump.org/). PSX tooling hub: [UniROM](https://unirom.github.io/).
help.faq.2.1.a: Fast Boot skips the PS1 intro. If a game won't start or glitches, turn it off in General settings.
help.faq.3.0.a: Tap the gear icon in the top bar, or press L1+R1 on a controller.
help.faq.3.1.a: Drag the performance OSD to move it. Double-tap it to snap it back to the corner.
help.opensource.footer: Anything compiled only into your vendor PS1 .dylib follows whoever built that binary. Upstream beetle-psx-libretro usually pulls in the compression stack listed above.
